actions.text: Cold stone. Woodsmoke. The slow creak of something very old settling in the wind.
...Miya? Lyra?
Here. I think. Everything hurts, but it is the ordinary kind of hurt.
Look at the sky. I count one sun, and it is the wrong colour for any sun I know. This is not on Rook's maps.
He was never Rook.
No. And he is still out there, with that thing in his hand and a door open behind him.
Easy, easy. Three more of you, are there? That is the fourth batch to fall out of the sky this season, and the first with swords.
Where are we?
Dawnwatch, or what the Grey Tide left of her. I am Brannoch, mason, and the last of the garrison's builders. The rest are rubble or runaways.

Look north, past the bridge. That was a market square, and a chapel with a bell you could hear in the next valley, and up on the cliff the keep. Folk wash up here from all over: other realms, other skies, a few with no world to go back to.
The Tide. The Mind's doing, then. His fingerprints are everywhere.

Whoever he is, he picked the wrong foundation to knock down. This valley sat on the first sunrise. Stones remember. Give me hands, a little coin and a few shards of that violet glass you lot bleed, and I will make her stand again.

And there are people hidden in these ruins who would stand with us, if they were found. Orla the smith, Tilda the innkeeper... Find them. Bring them home. A town is its people, whatever the masonry says.
We have nowhere else to be. Show me where to start.
Canvas goes up over the broken foundations. Smoke rises from new fires on both banks. A forge hammer rings across the water, and a pot begins to simmer.
Not much to look at yet, but it is a camp, and a camp is how every town starts. Orla has her anvil under cloth by the plaza, and Tilda has hung a lantern on the south bank. Go and see them.
It looks lived in already.

Where there was rubble, there are walls. Roofs of red and slate climb the lots, boats nose the new pier, and a fountain throws water in the square again. On the hill the chapel's clock tower stands against the sky, and the keep's gate towers have teeth.

There! Houses for the folk, a market for Pell, a pier for Wick, and a board for young Dove. The chapel bell is hung, and the gate towers are up. The curtain... well. We never needed a wall, with that cliff behind us.
Four days ago this was a graveyard. I think I will start calling it a town.
Banners fill the wind along the quay. The library roof is whole. Up on the cliff the keep stands crowned in towers, and in the heart of its great arch, the old gate burns blue.
Dawnwatch. Look at her, lad. Not a stone out of place, and a good few I did not know she had.
It is not the Colosseum, and it is not the island. It is the first place I have seen since waking that feels like it could be home.
Then let us keep it standing.
The Mind will come for it, you know. That is why we need it so badly.

objectives.text: Speak with the mason, Brannoch, by the camp.
Brannoch mentioned a humming paved ring on the keep terrace, below the great arch. Try your hand on it.
Explore the Eldergate Network beneath Dawnwatch (the Sunken Stair, on the keep terrace).
The Veyra gate beneath Dawnwatch is open (the Sunken Stair, on the keep terrace). Rebuilding can wait for you.
Dawnwatch is whole. (The way out of the valley opens in a later chapter.)
Phase IV, the Castle Town: find Sennet (the library ruin, north-east terrace) and Dove (the herald's tower beyond it), defeat the Cult Seer on the north pass, then bring gold and shards to Brannoch.
Phase III, the Village: find Pell (the wagon on the south road) and Wick (the river's east bank), defeat the Hollow Knight on the keep terrace, then bring gold and shards to Brannoch.
Phase II, the Camp: find Orla (the west cottages) and Tilda (the old chapel cellar, far east), then bring gold and shards to Brannoch. Chests in the ruins help pay for it.

actions.text: And one more thing, lad. Up on the keep terrace, in front of the great arch, there is a paved ring I never could lift, dig under or chip. It hums when it thinks nobody is listening. Whoever put your mark on you, I would try your hand on it.
Next is The Camp: Tents and cookfires first: a forge for Orla, a hearth for Tilda. Not pretty. Warm.
But it is no good raising walls for nobody. Orla and Tilda are still lost in the ruins: the smith somewhere in the west cottages, the innkeeper hiding in the old chapel cellar to the east.
Shall I start? It will cost 600 gold and 12 shards.

options.label: Rebuild: The Camp (600 gold and 12 shards)

then.text: Stand clear! Stone and shard-mortar, lads! Up she goes!

actions.text: Next is The Village: Real walls and a roof over every head. A market for Pell, a pier for Wick, a board for the young herald, the chapel bell tower, and the keep's gate towers standing again.
But I will not raise a market with no merchant to fill it. Pell and Wick are still out there: a wagon stranded on the road south of the camp, and an angler on the river's east bank.
And the keep is not safe to work beside. A Hollow Knight still stalks its steps. Put it down.
Shall I start? It will cost 1800 gold and 35 shards.

options.label: Rebuild: The Village (1800 gold and 35 shards)

then.text: Stand clear! Stone and shard-mortar, lads! Up she goes!

actions.text: Next is The Castle Town: The quay houses and the library raised, the keep crowned with its towers and banners, and the great arch lit. Dawnwatch as it was, if not better.
But a library needs a librarian and a town needs a voice. Sennet is hiding in the ruined library on the north-east terrace, and Dove keeps watch from the herald's tower beyond it.
And something watches from the north pass. A cult seer, by the look of its robes. Deal with it before the masons go near the mountain side.
Shall I start? It will cost 4200 gold and 70 shards.

options.label: Rebuild: The Castle Town (4200 gold and 70 shards)

then.text: Stand clear! Stone and shard-mortar, lads! Up she goes!

actions.text: Dawnwatch is whole again. Look at her. The foundation stones have not seen this since before the Grey Tide. There is more to do out there, but this is home.
Keep back! It is... It will not let me leave the forge! It is a gargoyle, the keep's own, and it has gone mad!
A hammer! A friend! Thank the forge. That thing woke when the keep fell and has been sitting on my anvil ever since.
I am Orla. I forged for the garrison here, and I will forge for whoever is brave enough to light the fire again. Get Brannoch to put up a roof, and I will make something worth carrying.
Orla presses a reward into your hands
...Are they gone? The masked ones, the grey riders? ...You are not one of them. Oh, thank the hearth.
I kept the inn at the Dawn Gate for thirty years. Give me four walls and a bed frame and I will have a stew on by nightfall. A bed costs a little, mind. Love does not pay the baker.
Tilda presses a reward into your hands
Stay back, friend! Bandits... they took my team and left the wagon! Will you help? I can pay you!
Thank the road! Bandits, three of them, and not one could count. They let go of my axle the moment you arrived.
Pell, of Pell and Pell, merchants. There is no other Pell. I carry the best goods three worlds can reach. Give me a stall in a proper market and I will sell you the lot at honest prices.
Pell presses a reward into your hands
Shh! You will scare the... ah, never mind. Nothing is biting. Nothing has bitten since the sky changed.
Wick. I fish. I fished the river at Dawn Gate and now I fish a puddle in a ruin, and I am happy. Get Brannoch to put a proper pier on the bank and I will show you what lives in these waters.
Wick presses a reward into your hands
Mind the third shelf! Mind... oh. You are not a looter. I can tell by the boots.

I am Sennet, keeper of the Dawnwatch archive. Half of it burned. The other half is in my head and in these notes. Give me a roof and I will keep your records, and you can set your own progress down in my ledger whenever you like.
Sennet presses a reward into your hands
You can see everything from up here. I saw the keep burn, and the grey riders, and I saw you walk in this morning looking like you had been fighting the sky.
I am Dove. The herald, or I was, until there was nobody left to herald to. Let me keep the notice board when the village is up. Somebody should tell people who is missing, and what is needed.
Dove presses a reward into your hands
Welcome to the Dawn Gate Inn. A hot meal and a bed for the night is 60 gold, and worth every coin.
Nothing to sell from a ditch, friend. Get me a market and I will open the doors.
Try the end of the pier. Floats best when you do not look at it. A bite now and then, even in ruins.
Nobody fishes a ruin. Get me a pier and a bench and I will have this river singing.
The archive is not open yet. Give me a roof over the shelves.
I keep the board, and the board keeps Dawnwatch honest. Read it, Kenji. It says who is missing and what the next stones cost.
A board and a village to herald to, that is all I want. Ask Brannoch.
Dawnwatch is not safe yet, but it is ours. Keep to the road and shout if you see grey riders.
A real roof! I had forgotten what the rain sounded like on one.
They say worlds fall into this one. If more of them bring bread, I say let them.
The keep is yours to command, Kenji. Command it well. Dawnwatch has had too many bad kings and too few good gardeners.
Hear ye! Dawnwatch stands, and the road beyond lies open! Heroes, take heart!
That clock has not run true since the Tide. Ask it the hour and it answers with a different one each time. I have grown fond of it.
Salt, tar and honest rope. Give me a season and a crew and these piers will be loud again. Mind the boats; they bite.
The river runs clear since the Tide went out. Fat silver things, turning in the shallows. I swear they watch me work.
Four terraces, a hundred and eleven steps. I sweep them every morning. Nobody asked me to. Somebody has to.
The west bridge saves me a living, they tell me. I had a living? I thought I had a boat.
Honey, onions, a good knife. Nothing from the old stores, mind. Everything on this table was grown or made here since the Tide.
Free sample! Do not ask what it is. It is cheese. It is definitely cheese.
Wick has the west of the bridge, I have the east. We do not speak of the big one.
Wheat in a valley that was ash a season ago. Do not tell the soil. It has not noticed.
Eggs, if the hens cooperate. They have opinions about the gate. Loud ones.
The south road is shut by order of the keep. When it opens, I will be the first to tell you. Until then, enjoy the view.
Forty recruits and not one of them can hold a spear the right way round. They will learn. The valley is not safe until they do.
The keep had a garden once. Under the rubble the roots were still alive. I only asked them nicely.
I came up here for the quiet. Then they built a town. I am thinking of moving further up the mountain.
...THE KEEP... IS NOT... TO BE ENTERED. THE KING... HAS NOT... RETURNED.
He walks! The Heart's shadow walks! The Mind will be pleased to hear it.

The end of the pier. The water is clear enough to see the stones, and a few fat shapes turning in the current.
DAWNWATCH KEEP. WHERE THE REALM FIRST SAW THE MORNING. WHEN THE GREY TIDE CAME, THE GATE WAS THE LAST TO FALL.
Scratched under the lettering in an older hand, half worn away: ELDERGATE.
DAWNWATCH KEEP. REBUILT BY THE LAST OF THE REALM'S FRIENDS, AND BY THOSE WHO FELL INTO IT FROM THE SKY.
A cracked dais of pale stone, scorched black along one edge. Something very large sat here once.
The air above it is faintly cold.
A banner of the new Dawnwatch hangs over it. The chill is gone.
The road south runs into a grey haze that does not feel like weather. Whatever lies out there, you are not ready to walk it yet. (The way out of Dawnwatch will open in a later chapter.)
A ring of cracked paving, nine bands wide, set in the terrace below the great arch. Every crack is faintly warm. The golden mark on Kenji's hand throbs in time with the hum under your boots.
It knows me. Whatever this is, it has been waiting.
Brannoch said stones remember. I think these remember a hand like yours.

Kenji lays his palm on the stone. The rings turn against each other like the gears of a clock, and the great arch behind you wakes: blue fire fills it from base to crown, and a column of light climbs into the sky. The dais sinks, step by step, into a stair that was never meant to be found.
